## Unsolicited advice

- **Be proactive about feedback/surfacing issues**
    - No [continuous feedback responses](https://forms.gle/8t232gDcbSxMpejU6) after first week and 3/10 non-responses to mandatory mid-course feedback
    - Future managers will not be as enthusiastic about soliciting information, but it is even more important for you to surface it then
- **Prioritize sleep**
    - [Giuntella et al (2026) JPE](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/740221) RCT nudged US college students to increase sleep, which on average causally increased sleep by 19 minutes/night and GPA by 0.08 points
- **Lean into struggle**
    - Independent research is hard, but you learn by doing and iterating

## Reminder on grade components

- 5% of grade is final code quality and replicability
    - Ensure code is reproducible as you go rather than trying to fix it up at the end
- 25% of grade is final exam
    - Ensure you understand your work as you go rather than "studying" at the end
    - Example question: "Referee suggests [X] would be a problem for your identification strategy. Explain why that is or isn't the case."

## Next assignment: initial paper draft
- Due date pushed to Tuesday 11/3 (1 day later than previous syllabus)
- No penalty for placeholders of planned results
    - But feedback will be better with actual results
- No bonus for length
    - Graded on the information you communicate, not the number of words it takes to do so
- Must include:
    1. Introduction
    2. Data section with (some) actual summary statistics
    3. Topic sentences for paragraphs with placeholder of planned results
